company.name: Meridian Compute
company.description: Operates three GPU clusters (pod-a, pod-b, pod-c) for internal ML teams. Internal platform services carry codenames that collide with public product names on purpose: a model without Meridian context will misroute them.

services.Loom: GPU interconnect fabric (NVLink, NVSwitch, InfiniBand). Public collision: Loom the video tool.
services.Vault: Parallel filesystem for datasets and checkpoints. Public collision: HashiCorp Vault (secrets).
services.Dispatch: Batch job scheduler built on Slurm.
services.Node Doctor: Node health daemon: GPU Xid, ECC, thermal, drain and reboot.
services.Backbone: Core network: DNS, BGP, zone-to-zone routing.
services.Gatekeeper: SSO and identity broker. Public collision: OPA Gatekeeper (Kubernetes admission).
services.Kite: Kubernetes control plane and image registry.
services.Beacon: Model inference serving layer. Public collision: Bluetooth beacons.
services.Ledger: Capacity, quota and reservation service. Public collision: accounting ledger.
services.Sentinel: Security incident response tooling. Public collision: Microsoft Sentinel.

runbooks.name: Loom link fault
runbooks.definition: NVLink, NVSwitch or InfiniBand link errors, flaps or degraded all-reduce performance.
runbooks.private_context: Training jobs reported as 'slow' on pod-b were a Loom link fault 8 times out of 10 last quarter, not a Dispatch problem. Policy: single-link flaps auto-remediate by draining the link; multi-node flaps page the Interconnect on-call. Response policy: S1 escalate to the incident commander; S2 page the on-call; S3, S4 let automation remediate.

runbooks.name: Vault filesystem
runbooks.definition: Vault read/write latency, metadata server pressure, mount failures, checkpoint write errors.
runbooks.private_context: Vault is the parallel filesystem, not the secrets manager. 'Permission denied' on a Vault path is almost always a stale mount or ACL sync lag, owned by Storage, never Identity or Security. Response policy: S1 escalate to the incident commander; S2, S3 page the on-call; S4 open a business-hours ticket.

runbooks.name: Dispatch queue
runbooks.definition: Jobs stuck pending, preemption loops, partition misconfiguration, scheduler daemon unresponsive.
runbooks.private_context: Dispatch owns scheduling only. A job that runs but runs slowly is not Dispatch. Jobs pending with 'Resources' reason on a cluster that looks idle usually means a Ledger reservation, so check RB-11 first. Response policy: S1 escalate to the incident commander; S2 page the on-call; S3, S4 open a business-hours ticket.

runbooks.name: Node Doctor GPU fault
runbooks.definition: GPU Xid errors, ECC errors, thermal throttling, node drained or rebooted by Node Doctor.
runbooks.private_context: Node Doctor auto-drains on Xid 79 and uncorrectable ECC; those are routine. More than five drains in an hour on one pod is a Loom or power event, escalate to incident commander. Response policy: S1 escalate to the incident commander; S2 page the on-call; S3, S4 let automation remediate.

runbooks.name: Backbone connectivity
runbooks.definition: DNS resolution failures, BGP session drops, zone-to-zone packet loss, routing table changes.
runbooks.private_context: Backbone is the core network. Anything inside a node (NVLink, IB) is Loom, not Backbone. Response policy: S1 escalate to the incident commander; S2, S3 page the on-call; S4 open a business-hours ticket.

runbooks.name: Gatekeeper auth
runbooks.definition: SSO login failures, token expiry storms, group membership sync lag, service account lockouts.
runbooks.private_context: Gatekeeper is the SSO broker, not the Kubernetes admission controller. Pods failing admission in Kite are RB-07. Unexpected login from a new country is RB-12, not RB-06. Response policy: S1, S2 page the on-call; S3, S4 open a business-hours ticket.

runbooks.name: Kite control plane
runbooks.definition: Kubernetes API latency, image pull failures, registry outages, admission webhook errors, etcd pressure.
runbooks.private_context: Image pull failures against the Kite registry are RB-07 even when the error text mentions 'unauthorized'; registry token refresh is owned by Container Platform. Response policy: S1 escalate to the incident commander; S2, S3 page the on-call; S4 open a business-hours ticket.

runbooks.name: Beacon serving
runbooks.definition: Model endpoint 5xx, p99 latency regression, model load failure after deploy, replica crash loops.
runbooks.private_context: Beacon is the model serving layer. 'Beacon timeouts' are never a network problem; 9 of the last 10 were a bad deploy, so the action is rollback and page Inference Serving. Response policy: S1 escalate to the incident commander; S2, S3 page the on-call; S4 open a business-hours ticket.

runbooks.name: Conveyor pipeline
runbooks.definition: ETL job failures, schema drift, upstream data late, pipeline lag beyond SLA.
runbooks.private_context: Conveyor failures are business-hours tickets unless a training launch depends on the output today, in which case page. Response policy: S1, S2 page the on-call; S3, S4 open a business-hours ticket.

runbooks.name: Lantern telemetry
runbooks.definition: Missing metrics, alert storms from a broken rule, dashboards blank, log ingestion lag.
runbooks.private_context: 'No GPU metrics for node X' is a Lantern exporter crash, not a node fault, unless Node Doctor also reports the node. Check Node Doctor before paging anyone. Response policy: S1 page the on-call; S2, S3, S4 open a business-hours ticket.

runbooks.name: Ledger capacity
runbooks.definition: Quota exceeded, reservation conflicts, allocation denied, budget threshold alerts.
runbooks.private_context: Ledger is the capacity and quota service, nothing to do with finance or billing systems. Ledger issues never page; they are tickets. Response policy: S1, S2, S3, S4 open a business-hours ticket.

runbooks.name: Sentinel security event
runbooks.definition: Suspicious logins, credential leaks, unexpected egress, privilege escalation attempts.
runbooks.private_context: Any Sentinel finding escalates to the incident commander regardless of severity. A leaked key found in a repo is RB-12 even if the key belongs to Vault or Gatekeeper. Response policy: S1, S2, S3, S4 escalate to the incident commander.

actions.definition: Run the runbook's automated fix and notify the team channel. No human paged.
Page the owning team's on-call engineer now.
Open a ticket for the owning team; handled during business hours.
Declare an incident and page the incident commander.

reporter_styles.description: Terse automated alert text with metric names, thresholds and a node or service identifier. One to three lines.
Informal message from an engineer in the ops channel. Lowercase, abbreviations, missing details, maybe a guess at the cause.
Structured ticket with Summary, Impact, Steps taken and Request sections.
Machine-generated alert payload with fields like alertname, labels, annotations and firing time, rendered as compact JSON.

holdout_families.note: One family per runbook is held out of training entirely and appears only in the test set, so the test measures generalization across scenario types rather than memorization.

family_descriptions.nvlink-flap: an NVLink link on one node keeps going down and coming back up; GPU-to-GPU bandwidth drops while it happens
family_descriptions.ib-port-errors: InfiniBand port counters on a node or switch show symbol errors and link downs climbing
family_descriptions.slow-allreduce-training-job: a multi-node training job is running but much slower than usual; collective operations take several times longer; nothing is queued or failing
family_descriptions.nvswitch-reset-loop: an NVSwitch keeps resetting itself every few minutes, taking a whole node's GPU fabric with it
family_descriptions.vault-mds-latency: metadata operations on the shared filesystem (ls, open, stat) are taking seconds instead of milliseconds
family_descriptions.checkpoint-write-enospc: training checkpoints fail to write with out-of-space errors on the shared filesystem even though quota looked fine
family_descriptions.vault-mount-permission-denied: nodes get permission denied on shared filesystem paths that worked yesterday; mounts look stale
family_descriptions.vault-scrub-degraded: the shared filesystem reports a degraded storage target and a background scrub is running; throughput is down
family_descriptions.jobs-pending-no-reason: jobs sit in pending with no useful reason while the cluster has idle nodes
family_descriptions.preemption-loop: a job keeps getting preempted and requeued over and over, never finishing
family_descriptions.partition-down: a scheduler partition shows down or drained and nothing is dispatching to it
family_descriptions.slurmctld-unresponsive: the scheduler controller daemon stops answering; job commands hang or time out
family_descriptions.xid-79-fallen-off-bus: a GPU reports Xid 79, has fallen off the bus, and the node was drained automatically
family_descriptions.ecc-uncorrectable: a GPU logs an uncorrectable ECC error; the running job died and the node was drained
family_descriptions.thermal-throttle: GPUs on a node are hitting thermal limits and clocking down; throughput drops
family_descriptions.node-doctor-drain-storm: many nodes in one pod get drained within a short window by the health daemon
family_descriptions.dns-resolution-failures: hostnames stop resolving intermittently inside a zone; connections fail by name but work by IP
family_descriptions.bgp-session-flap: a core router's BGP session keeps dropping and re-establishing; traffic between zones blips
family_descriptions.zone-packet-loss: steady packet loss between two availability zones; latency spikes on cross-zone traffic
family_descriptions.route-leak: routes that should stay internal show up where they do not belong; some traffic takes a wrong path
family_descriptions.sso-login-loop: users are bounced back to the login page repeatedly after signing in
family_descriptions.token-expiry-storm: a wave of access tokens expire at once; service calls fail with unauthorized until re-auth
family_descriptions.group-sync-lag: group membership changes take far longer than usual to show up; new team members cannot access what they should
family_descriptions.service-account-lockout: an automation's service account gets locked out after repeated failed auth attempts
family_descriptions.image-pull-backoff-registry: pods are stuck pulling images from the internal registry; pull backoff errors, sometimes unauthorized
family_descriptions.apiserver-latency: Kubernetes API calls are slow; kubectl and controllers time out
family_descriptions.admission-webhook-timeout: pods fail to be created because an admission webhook times out
family_descriptions.etcd-disk-pressure: the cluster's etcd reports disk pressure or high fsync latency; the control plane gets flaky
family_descriptions.endpoint-5xx-after-deploy: a model endpoint started returning 5xx errors right after a new version rolled out
family_descriptions.p99-latency-regression: a model endpoint's tail latency jumped several-fold with no error increase
family_descriptions.model-load-oom: new replicas of a model crash on startup running out of GPU memory while loading weights
family_descriptions.replica-crashloop: model serving replicas keep restarting; the endpoint is partially available
family_descriptions.schema-drift-upstream: an upstream data source changed its schema and the ingestion job now fails on parsing
family_descriptions.pipeline-lag-sla: a data pipeline is running but far behind schedule; downstream datasets are stale
family_descriptions.etl-task-oom: a transform task in a data pipeline is killed for using too much memory
family_descriptions.late-partition: an expected daily data partition has not arrived; downstream jobs are waiting on it
family_descriptions.gpu-metrics-gap-exporter: GPU metrics for a node or pod vanished from dashboards while the GPUs themselves run fine
family_descriptions.alert-storm-bad-rule: a newly changed alert rule is firing hundreds of times for a condition that is not real
family_descriptions.dashboard-blank: monitoring dashboards show no data though services are up
family_descriptions.log-ingestion-lag: logs arrive in the logging system many minutes late; searches miss recent events
family_descriptions.quota-exceeded-team: a team hit its GPU quota and new jobs are rejected
family_descriptions.reservation-conflict: two reservations overlap on the same nodes and one of them cannot start
family_descriptions.allocation-denied: a request for GPUs is denied for lack of available capacity in the reservation
family_descriptions.budget-threshold: a team crossed a spending or usage threshold and got a warning
family_descriptions.impossible-travel-login: a user account logged in from two distant countries within minutes
family_descriptions.leaked-api-key: a secret or API key was found committed to a repository
family_descriptions.unexpected-egress: a node is sending an unusual volume of data to an external address
family_descriptions.privilege-escalation: a process or user gained elevated privileges in a way policy does not allow

policy_note: Actions are a deterministic function of runbook and severity (see runbooks[].policy). Severity S1 is a production outage, S2 serious and active, S3 real but contained, S4 a heads-up.
